sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that all worlds depend on the precision of a mitzvah, using the examples of sacrifice (elevation) and tefillin (drawing down), and clarifies that this dependence proves the worlds are nullified before a single detail of Torah.

translations.translation: The explanation is,
it is brought in Iggeret HaKodesh, the discourse beginning "Dovid, songs are called to You,"59
that all the upper and lower worlds are dependent on the precision of a mitzvah,
and he brings two examples for this,
a sacrifice and tefillin.
And my master, my father, the Rebbe, explains in his glosses to the Tanya,60
that the reason he seized upon these two mitzvos
(a sacrifice and tefillin)
is,
because the general concept of the mitzvos is elevation and drawing down,
ratzo and shov
(as is explained in Likkutei Torah, in the discourse beginning "This is the statute of the Torah"61),
and therefore he seized upon these two mitzvos,
for a sacrifice is elevation,
ratzo,
and tefillin is drawing down,
shov
(as is explained in Likkutei Torah, in the discourses on the libations62).
And it is necessary to understand,
what relevance does the matter explained in the aforementioned Iggeret HaKodesh
[that all worlds are dependent on the precision of a mitzvah]
have to the hint that the concept of the mitzvos is elevation and drawing down?
And it may be said,

that this which is explained in Iggeret HaKodesh, that all worlds are dependent on the precision of a mitzvah, is an introduction to what is stated there afterwards, that all worlds are nullified in existence relative to one detail of the details of Torah.
For this that Dovid said,63
"Songs were Your statutes to me," etc., is praise of the Torah
(as is explained in the aforementioned Iggeret HaKodesh at its beginning),
and the praise is that all worlds are nullified in existence
(and not merely dependent)64
relative to one detail of the details of Torah,
except that the revelation of this matter of Torah is through the fact that all worlds are dependent on the precision of a mitzvah.
And this is,
that regarding the mitzvos, which are commandments to man as to how he should conduct himself in the world,
there must necessarily be some value and place-occupancy to the worlds,
and this that the worlds are nullified in existence is
(specifically)
relative to
(one detail of the details of)
Torah.
And the proof of this is from the fact that all worlds are dependent on the precision of a mitzvah.
For this that the worlds are dependent on the precision of a mitzvah
(even on a light precision)
is because it is a precision of Torah,
relative to which the worlds are nullified in existence,
and therefore,
even after it is drawn down into mitzvos and becomes a "precision of a mitzvah,"
all the worlds are dependent upon it.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the examples of sacrifice and tefillin in Iggeret HaKodesh hint that even after Torah's details are drawn into mitzvos, the concepts of elevation (ratzo) and return (shov) reveal their supernal source, as reflected in the blessing over mitzvos.

translations.translation: And in order to explain that even after the drawing down of the details of Torah into the mitzvos, the matter of Torah shines within them in revelation,
[the author of] Iggeret HaKodesh hints
(by bringing the examples of a sacrifice and tefillin)
that the concept of the mitzvos is elevation and drawing down,
ratzo and shov.
For it may be said,
that the concept of the elevation and ratzo in the mitzvos is that their source is felt within them as they are in the Torah, which is above the world,
and the concept of the drawing down and shov in them is that they are drawn down to be commandments to man,
and even then, it is felt within them that their source is in the Torah, which is above worlds
[for the concept of ratzo and shov is that even after the shov, the impression of the ratzo is recognizable65].
And one may take note from this of what we say in the blessing over mitzvos, "Who sanctified us with His mitzvos and commanded us,"
for it may be said,
that "Who sanctified us with His mitzvos" is the matter of elevation,
that He elevated us to the level of the supernal Holy of Holies, blessed be He, which is the holiness of the Holy One, blessed be He, in His glory and in His very Self,66
and "and commanded us" is the matter of drawing down,
that He commanded us.
And the reason for this, that we say in the blessing over mitzvos
(regarding the mitzvos that were given to us)
"Who sanctified us with His mitzvos,"
is,
because even after He commanded us
(and they became commandments to man)
they are His mitzvos of the Holy One, blessed be He, just as He is holy and separate from the matter of commanding to man.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that through the Torah, pleasure is drawn into the service of accepting the yoke in mitzvah observance, because the Torah reveals that man's separate existence itself fulfills the supernal intent, so his nullification is complete and not contradictory to pleasure.

translations.translation: And this is that through the Torah, pleasure is drawn down even into the service of accepting the yoke in the fulfillment of the mitzvos.
For this that the fulfillment of the mitzvos is in a manner of accepting the yoke, like a servant who fulfills the command of the king
[that the servant is not the master, but rather he is nullified to the master]
is because the intent in the matter of the mitzvos
(commandments to man)
is that man should be an existence separate from Him
(who has no pleasure in Divinity)
and nevertheless be nullified to Him.
And through the drawing down of the Torah
(which is above the command to man)
into the mitzvos and into the service of accepting the yoke
(for the Torah said, "and you shall serve"),
it is felt,
that this that man is an existence separate from Him, blessed be He, is in order to complete the supernal intent.
And through this,
the nullification of accepting the yoke is in his entire existence,
meaning that even this that he became like an existence for himself is in order to complete the intent.
And therefore, his existence is not a contradiction to the pleasure he has in his service
(i.e., to the pleasure of the Master that is drawn into him),
because even his existence is in order to complete the intent.
